title: IM Draft Angle — ISO 10724
body: Minimum draft angle for injection moulding: 0.5° for cosmetic/unpainted surfaces, 1.0° standard, 1.5° minimum for textured/EDM surfaces, 3° for deep ribs. Insufficient draft causes drag marks, ejection damage, and increased cycle time.

title: IM Gate Types — SPI Gating Guidelines
body: Hot-tip gate: preferred for engineering resins (PA, PC, POM, PBT) — eliminates gate vestige and regrind. Sub-gate (tunnel/banana): self-degating, good for PP/PE/ABS. Edge gate: simplest, leaves witness mark. Fan gate: reduces weld lines on thin walls. Valve gate: best surface finish, highest tooling cost.

title: IM Wall Thickness — SPI Design Guide
body: PA66: nominal 2.0–3.0 mm, min 0.8 mm, max 4.0 mm. PP: 0.8–3.0 mm. PC: 0.75–3.5 mm. ABS: 1.2–3.5 mm. Non-uniform walls cause sink marks, warpage, and longer cycle times. Rib thickness: 50–60% of adjacent wall. Boss OD: 2–2.5× wall.

title: IM Clamp Force — Engineering Rule
body: Clamp force (tonnes) = projected area (cm²) × cavity pressure factor. Factor: 0.35 t/cm² thin-wall PP, 0.5 t/cm² standard ABS/PP, 0.7 t/cm² engineering resins (PA/PC), 1.0 t/cm² high-viscosity materials. Add 15% safety margin. Exceeding machine clamp force causes flash.

title: Sheet Metal Bend Radius — DIN 6935
body: Minimum inside bend radius = 1× material thickness for mild steel, 1.5× for stainless steel, 2× for aluminium 5052. Tighter radii cause outer fibre cracking. Bend deduction ≈ 0.43× thickness for 90° bends (varies by tool radius).

title: CNC Tolerances — ASME Y14.5
body: Standard CNC milling tolerance: ±0.1 mm (IT9). Fine finish: ±0.025 mm (IT7). Grinding: ±0.005 mm (IT5). Surface finish: Ra 3.2 µm standard turning, Ra 0.8 µm finish turning, Ra 0.4 µm grinding. Tighter tolerances multiply cycle time and increase inspection cost significantly.

title: Injection Moulding Shrinkage — SPI
body: Material shrinkage rates: PP 1.5–2.5%, PA66 (dry) 0.8–1.5%, PA66 (conditioned) 1.5–2.5%, ABS 0.4–0.7%, PC 0.5–0.7%, POM 1.9–2.3%. Higher shrinkage = larger mould cavities required and tighter process control. Anisotropic shrinkage causes warpage in thin or asymmetric parts.

title: Die Casting Design Rules
body: Aluminium die casting: min wall 1.0 mm, draft 1–3°, fillets min 0.8 mm radius. Zinc: min wall 0.4 mm, higher precision. Clamp force: 1.0–1.5 t/cm² of projected area. Porosity risk increases with wall >5 mm or poorly vented die. Tooling life: 50k–200k shots (Al), 500k+ shots (Zn).

title: Undercut Detection — IM Tooling
body: Undercuts parallel to mould open direction require side actions (lifters, slides, collapsible cores). Side actions add $3k–$15k per action to tooling cost and 15–25% to cycle time. Internal undercuts require collapsible cores (+$5k–20k). Design review should eliminate undercuts or plan for split tooling before design freeze.

title: Surface Finish Standards — ISO 1302
body: Ra 25 µm: rough machining. Ra 6.3 µm: general machining. Ra 3.2 µm: standard turned/milled. Ra 1.6 µm: fine machining. Ra 0.8 µm: fine turning or grinding. Ra 0.4 µm: precision grinding. Ra 0.1 µm: lapping/super-finishing. Each step tighter approximately doubles machining time.

title: Sheet Metal Hole-to-Edge Rules
body: Minimum hole-to-edge distance: 2× material thickness. Minimum hole diameter: 1× material thickness (punching), 0.5× (laser). Hole-to-hole minimum: 2× thickness. Violating these rules causes burring, tear-out, and fixture issues. Laser can achieve tighter spacings than punch.

title: Anodising Design Rules — MIL-A-8625
body: Type II (decorative): 0.005–0.025 mm coating thickness. Type III (hard): 0.025–0.075 mm. Anodising adds to all surfaces including threads (design for undersize by coating thickness). Masking areas adds cost. Best on 6061/6063 Al; 7075 and 2024 give lower quality coatings.
